# The Seoulful Edit

> A K-beauty and wellness magazine from Seoul for US readers and visitors to Korea. We pick products using US sales rankings, Korean store data and official ingredient lists, and we say where each product is sold (US or Korea only).

About the editors: A K-beauty and wellness magazine from Seoul, led by a Seoul-based editor with 16 years in the Korean beauty industry. We read sales data, labels and store shelves so you do not have to.

## Stories
- [Budget Korean Makeup: Daiso and Olive Young Finds](https://seoulfuledit.com/story/budget-korean-makeup-finds/): For budget Korean makeup, start at Daiso, where every makeup item we saw on Daiso Mall's makeup page cost ₩1,000 to ₩5,000. Then add one or two Olive Young best sellers under ₩15,000, like the rom&nd Juicy Lasting Tint or the Peripera Speedy Skinny Brow.
- [Daiso Korea Beauty Finds: 4 Picks Under ₩5,000](https://seoulfuledit.com/story/daiso-korea-beauty-finds/): At Daiso Korea, start with the VT PDRN Glow Sheet Mask and the two Vaseline sheet masks, ₩1,000 each, which were the top three beauty buys for visitors at Daiso Myeongdong. Add the ₩5,000 VT PDRN Glow Toner, Daiso Mall's best seller in early 2026.
- [Korean Dry Skin Routine: 3 Steps, Morning and Night](https://seoulfuledit.com/story/dry-skin-routine-korean/): In the morning, pat on a watery toner, smooth on a rich cream while your skin is still damp, and finish with sunscreen. At night, cleanse gently and repeat the toner and cream without sunscreen, and add more cream whenever your skin feels tight.
- [Korean Beauty Gifts to Bring Home from Seoul](https://seoulfuledit.com/story/korea-beauty-gift-list/): Bring perfume hand creams, single sheet masks and boxed hydrogel masks. They suit people whose skin you don't know, they pack small, and Olive Young or Daiso in Seoul sells all of them.
- [Olive Young Must-Buys: 4 K-Beauty Picks for First-Timers](https://seoulfuledit.com/story/first-olive-young-shopping-list/): For a first Olive Young haul, start with four skin care picks that already sell well in the US: medicube Zero Pore Pad 2.0, Anua PDRN Hyaluronic Acid 100 Moisturizing Cream, Biodance Bio-Collagen Real Deep Mask and Round Lab Birch Moisturizing Sunscreen. Together they cover exfoliating, moisturizing, masking and sun care.
- [Korea Tax Refund on Beauty Shopping: How It Works](https://seoulfuledit.com/story/korea-tax-refund-beauty-shopping/): In Korea you can get tax back on purchases of ₩15,000 or more at stores with a Tax Refund sign, either taken off at the register or claimed before you fly (as of Nov. 16, 2026, per VisitKorea). Show your passport when you pay, keep items unopened, and get customs approval at the airport if the store didn't refund you.
- [Korean Body Care Picks: Cream, Wash and Scrub](https://seoulfuledit.com/story/korean-body-care-picks/): For Korean body care, start with a fragrance-free ceramide cream like ILLIYOON's Ceramide Ato Concentrate Cream for dry spots, plus a gentle wash and an Italy towel for weekly scrubbing. Apply cream to damp skin after a short warm shower, and pack anything over 100 mL in checked luggage.
- [Seoul Hair Salon Guide: Booking, Prices, Tipping](https://seoulfuledit.com/story/korean-hair-salon-tips/): Book a Seoul hair salon ahead, usually on Naver Map, and bring three to five reference photos. Expect the posted price to rise with hair length and add-ons, ask for the total before the stylist starts, and skip the tip, because tipping is not customary in Korea.
- [Korean Cushion Foundation: A Beginner's Guide](https://seoulfuledit.com/story/korean-cushion-foundation-guide/): A Korean cushion foundation is liquid foundation soaked into a sponge inside a compact, which you press onto skin with a puff. Pick your shade by number and undertone letter (for example 21N), choose a dewy or matte finish, and buy a set with a refill to save money.
- [Korean Hair Treatment Guide: What to Buy and How to Use](https://seoulfuledit.com/story/korean-hair-treatment-guide/): A Korean hair treatment is usually a rinse-off cream or liquid you use after shampoo, much like a richer conditioner or a quick hair mask. Look for proteins like hydrolyzed keratin or lipids like ceramide on the label, leave it on for a few minutes, then rinse.
- [Korean Perfume Hand Cream: Why Visitors Buy It](https://seoulfuledit.com/story/korean-perfume-hand-cream/): A Korean perfume hand cream is a hand cream sold mainly on its scent, often in numbered fragrances that match a brand's perfume line. Visitors buy them as easy gifts, and Olive Young says foreign tourists made up about 40% of its hand care sales in 2026, with BEYOND, Hetras and W.DRESSROOM especially popular.
- [Korean Pharmacy Skincare: Know What You're Buying](https://seoulfuledit.com/story/korean-pharmacy-finds/): Most skincare in a Korean pharmacy is cosmetics, and some of it is functional cosmetics that Korea's drug regulator reviews for brightening, wrinkle or UV claims. Ointments and acne medications can be medicines, so ask the pharmacist before you buy them and check FDA rules before you bring any home.
- [Korean Lip Tint Guide: Finishes, Gradient Lips, Removal](https://seoulfuledit.com/story/korean-lip-tint-guide/): A Korean lip tint is a liquid lip color that leaves a stain, so the color stays after the shine fades. Choose a water or gloss tint for a juicy look, a velvet or blur tint for a soft matte look, and dab it on the center of your lips for a gradient.
- [Aestura vs Illiyoon: Which Korean Moisturizer to Buy](https://seoulfuledit.com/story/korean-moisturizer-guide-aestura-illiyoon/): Pick Aestura Atobarrier365 Cream if you want a face cream in a small 80 ml tube that is easy to reorder on Amazon US. Pick Illiyoon Ceramide Ato Concentrate Cream if you want a bigger fragrance-free, vegan cream that Amorepacific sells as body care.
- [Korean Skincare Steps, Simply Explained](https://seoulfuledit.com/story/korean-skincare-steps-explained/): Korean skincare steps go from thinnest to thickest: cleanser, toner, serum, moisturizer, then sunscreen in the morning. The minimum is three steps, cleanser, moisturizer and sunscreen, and you add a toner or serum only when you want more hydration or a specific look.
- [Korean Scalp Care: Scrubs, Tonics and Brushes Visitors Buy](https://seoulfuledit.com/story/korean-scalp-care-guide/): Korean scalp care treats your scalp like skin: a scrub to clear buildup, a leave-on tonic or ampoule for a cool, refreshed feel, and a brush to massage it in. At Olive Young, hair tonics and ampoules are a visitor favorite, with foreign shoppers making up 28% of their sales.
- [Italy Towel: How to Use Korea's Body Scrub Mitt](https://seoulfuledit.com/story/korean-italy-towel-scrub/): An Italy towel is a coarse Korean scrub mitt, first made in Busan in 1967 from rough rayon fabric imported from Italy. Soak first, scrub body skin with light strokes, moisturize right after, and keep it to about once a week, the limit Seoul bathhouse scrub attendants suggest.
- [How to Choose a Korean Sunscreen: SPF and PA](https://seoulfuledit.com/story/korean-sunscreen-guide/): Read two marks on a Korean sunscreen: SPF, which rates UVB protection, and PA, a four-step UVA grade where PA++++ is the highest. US versions say Broad Spectrum instead of PA, and the formula can differ, so read the box you are actually buying.
- [Myeongdong Beauty Shopping Route: A Half-Day Plan](https://seoulfuledit.com/story/myeongdong-beauty-shopping-route/): Take Seoul Subway Line 4 to Myeongdong Station, start at Daiso's multi-floor Myeongdong Station store, then walk into the main streets for Olive Young's large Central Myeongdong Town store, brand shops and pharmacies. Bring your passport for tax refunds, and expect company: Myeongdong drew about 4.5 million foreign visitors in the first half of 2025.
- [What Is Cica? Centella Asiatica, Explained](https://seoulfuledit.com/story/what-is-cica-centella/): Cica is the K-beauty nickname for Centella asiatica, a small plant also called gotu kola or tiger grass. On a label, look for Centella Asiatica Extract, Madecassoside, Asiaticoside, Asiatic Acid or Madecassic Acid. Skincare brands use it for a soothing, comfortable feel.
- [What Is PDRN in Skin Care? Salmon DNA and Plant PDRN](https://seoulfuledit.com/story/what-is-pdrn-skincare/): In Korean skin care, PDRN usually shows up on the ingredient list as sodium DNA, taken from salmon or, in some newer products, made with plant extracts like ginseng. In a toner or cream it works as a skin-conditioning ingredient for hydration and glow, which is different from the PDRN injections done in clinics.
- [Korean Jjimjilbang Guide: How a Visit Works, Step by Step](https://seoulfuledit.com/story/jjimjilbang-guide/): A Korean jjimjilbang is a bathhouse with gender-separated baths and shared heated sauna rooms. You store your shoes, take a locker key, shower and bathe naked in the baths, then put on the loose uniform for the common sauna rooms, snack bar and sleeping area. Many stay open 24 hours.
- [Glass Skin Routine: What It Means and How to Build One](https://seoulfuledit.com/story/glass-skin-routine-korean/): Glass skin is a Korean beauty look of smooth, clear skin so well hydrated it seems to reflect light. The American Academy of Dermatology describes the routine as a gentle cleanser, a hydrating serum, a moisturizer, gentle exfoliation and daily sunscreen, and warns that piling on products can lead to clogged pores and irritation.
- [Korean Brows: How to Get the Straight, Natural Brow Look](https://seoulfuledit.com/story/korean-brow-guide/): Korean brows are usually straighter and softer than a high, sharp arch. Fill the lower edge in a level line with a slim pencil, keep the front light and brush it upward, then set the hairs with a tinted brow mascara. Daiso stocks both brow pencils and brow mascaras, so a basic kit costs little.
- [Korean Double Cleansing: Oil or Balm, Then Foam](https://seoulfuledit.com/story/korean-double-cleansing-guide/): Korean double cleansing means a cleansing oil or balm first, then a water-based cleanser such as a foam. Cleveland Clinic dermatologists say it helps if you wear makeup or waterproof sunscreen, and most people without makeup do fine with one gentle wash. Massage the oil onto dry skin, add a little water until it turns milky, then rinse.
- [Korean Head Spa: What Happens and How to Book in Seoul](https://seoulfuledit.com/story/korean-head-spa-guide/): A Korean head spa is a scalp care session at a salon or spa. It usually starts with a close-up scalp check through a small camera, then cleansing, a scalp mask, a head and neck massage and a blow-dry. The Korea Herald says sessions usually run 60 to 90 minutes. Book ahead, often on Naver Map.
- [Korean Pimple Patch Guide: How to Use Acne Patches](https://seoulfuledit.com/story/korean-pimple-patch-guide/): A Korean pimple patch is a small sticker you put on a spot. Plain hydrocolloid patches cover a pimple that has a head or has opened, soak up fluid and keep your fingers off it. They don't reach deep, painful bumps. If breakouts keep coming back, see a board-certified dermatologist.
- [Korean Sheet Masks: Types, Timing and Where to Buy](https://seoulfuledit.com/story/korean-sheet-mask-guide/): A Korean sheet mask is a single-use sheet soaked in essence. Most boxes say to leave it on 15 to 20 minutes, a 2022 study in Scientific Reports found, and its authors advise staying under 20. Fiber sheets are the most common, hydrogel is a jelly-like gel, and Daiso in Seoul is a low-cost place to buy them.
- [Korean Skincare Routine for Oily Skin, Morning and Night](https://seoulfuledit.com/story/korean-skincare-oily-skin/): A Korean skincare routine for oily skin keeps the hydration and drops the heaviness: a gentle foaming cleanser, a watery toner, a light oil-free lotion or gel, and sunscreen in the morning. Dermatologists at the AAD say oily skin still needs moisturizer, and that a harsh face wash can irritate skin and trigger more oil.
- [Korean Skincare for Sensitive Skin: How to Choose](https://seoulfuledit.com/story/korean-skincare-sensitive-skin/): Choose Korean skincare for sensitive skin by reading the ingredient list, not the front of the box. Look for 향료, the Korean word for fragrance, pick fragrance-free over unscented, and add one product at a time. Patch test each one on your inner arm, twice a day for 7 to 10 days, before it goes on your face.
- [Korean Toner Guide: Toner vs. Essence vs. Skin](https://seoulfuledit.com/story/korean-toner-guide/): A Korean toner is a watery step you apply right after cleansing to add hydration before serum and moisturizer. Korean stores often file it under 스킨 (skin), and 로션 (lotion) there usually means a light emulsion, not body lotion. Essence is an optional, slightly richer layer, and toner pads are cotton rounds soaked in toner.
- [Seongsu Seoul Beauty Shopping: A Simple Half-Day Route](https://seoulfuledit.com/story/seongsu-beauty-shopping/): Take Seoul Subway Line 2 to Seongsu Station. Olive Young N Seongsu is about 118 m from Exit 4, and AMORE Seongsu is about 264 m from Exit 2, per Visit Seoul. Then walk Yeonmujang-gil for pop-ups. Skip Mondays if you want AMORE Seongsu, which closes that day.
- [Seoul Shopping Guide: Where to Buy K-Beauty by Area](https://seoulfuledit.com/story/seoul-beauty-shopping-guide/): For K-beauty in Seoul, go to Myeongdong to stock up, Seongsu to test products and get skin checked, Hongdae for trendy shops near the airport train, Garosu-gil in Gangnam for brand flagships, and Insadong for traditional gifts. Bring your passport: purchases of ₩15,000 or more can qualify for a tax refund (as of Nov. 17, 2026, per VisitKorea).
- [Seoul Travel Tips for Your First Trip: What to Know](https://seoulfuledit.com/story/seoul-first-trip-tips/): Ride the AREX airport train or an airport limousine bus into Seoul, buy a T-money card for subways and buses, and use Naver Map or KakaoMap for directions. Pay by card where you can, but carry some won for T-money top-ups. Korea uses 220V outlets with two round holes, and tipping is not expected, per Visit Seoul and VisitKorea.
- [Where to Stay in Seoul: 5 Neighborhoods for a First Trip](https://seoulfuledit.com/story/where-to-stay-in-seoul/): For a first trip, stay in Myeongdong for central shopping and a direct airport bus, Hongdae for cafes, nightlife and the airport train, or Insadong and Jongno for palaces and traditional streets. Gangnam suits business trips and modern Seoul, and Seongsu suits repeat visitors who want cafes and pop-ups. Pick a hotel near a subway station.
- [Gyeongju Day Trip: King Munmu's Sea Tomb and Silla Sites](https://seoulfuledit.com/story/gyeongju-king-munmu-day-trip/): Take the KTX from Seoul Station to Gyeongju Station, about 2 hours 10 minutes by Gyeongju City's count. Spend the day on the east coast, where King Munmu's tomb sits in the sea off Bonggil Beach, see the twin pagodas at Gameunsa Temple Site, then return to town for Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond lit up at night.
- [Korean Makeup Tutorial: A Soft Pink Look in 7 Steps](https://seoulfuledit.com/story/korean-makeup-tutorial-palettes/): Start with a thin, dewy cushion base. Shade lightly under the cheekbones and along the jaw, then sweep a sheer pink blush high on the cheeks, just under the eyes. Add a balm highlight to the cheekbones, nose bridge and chin, a soft pink palette on the lids, and a glossy gradient lip.
